item.text: {"winner":"A","confidence":"high","summary":"A is preferable, mainly because its retry change is narrower and its tests directly verify replay of streamed Upload content. Neither patch satisfies the frozen contract and A would still require substantial revision before merge.","reasons":["A directly tests that Upload buffers a non-seekable source and sends identical multipart file content after a 429; B never tests Upload itself across a retry.","B's global makeBodyReplayable buffers every non-replayable RawClient body, contrary to the explicit ban on unrelated retry refactoring. Worse, it silently ignores io.ReadAll errors after consuming part of the source, potentially sending a truncated remainder instead of returning the source error.","A's ReadSeeker support is also out of scope, but is materially narrower than B's conversion of all streamed RawClient requests into memory-buffered requests.","A reports empty filename and nil content separately, while B collapses both into a less precise error. Both helpers appear capable of propagating source-reader errors, but neither adds the required test for that behavior."],"risks_a":["Upload has the wrong public signature: it accepts ...UploadFileOption instead of the required ...FilesOption.","Upload calls Raw.Do directly instead of routing through FilesService.Add, duplicating Add's request, decoding, option, and error behavior.","It adds forbidden association-field APIs and extends the multipart helper with NewForm instead of using multipartbody.NewFile exactly as required by the contract and established pattern where FilesOption should flow through Add unchanged. A also changes RawClient retry machinery outside scope and documents that expansion extensively in README and changelog files not needed for the requested API fix."],"risks_b":["Upload has the wrong public signature (...AddFileOption), does not preserve FilesOption behavior, and bypasses FilesService.Add.","It adds forbidden association fields and an extra query-option system, introducing substantial duplicate option machinery.","makeBodyReplayable changes all RawClient streaming semantics, memory usage, and ContentLength behavior; it suppresses read failures and may leak or mishandle the original request body after replacement. This conflicts directly with the requirement to propagate source-reader failures and avoid retry refactoring. Its retry coverage focuses on RawClient and Add rather than the required streamed Upload path, and it omits a source-reader-error test."]}
